candidatePrimary.transactional: pipeline<transaction: {isolation:..., access:...}> tx = provider { ... commit value }
candidatePrimary.keyword: Historical hypothesis: the transaction keyword could be removed before 1.0; W-1511 now rejects the standalone source form.
candidatePrimary.plainCommit: Exports an output envelope and does not imply rollback.
candidatePrimary.transactionalCommit: Also requests an atomic provider commit.
candidatePrimary.defaults: Isolation, access, provider capability and failure defaults remain evidence questions; no default is ratified by this ledger.

forks.hypothesis: Restrict the current transaction body to a static dependent-call DAG and move dynamic control into a provider method.
forks.risk: A remote branch or loop may become hidden provider behavior, weakening source-visible ownership, diagnostics and cancellation boundaries.
evidenceRequired: HIR schema for static transaction nodes
provider contract for dynamic control and commit acknowledgement
Last Light migration and diagnostic examples

forks.hypothesis: One pipeline keyword selects a mode-dependent body shape and terminal contract over a StructuredOperationRegion; each mode has its own terminal, with the candidate primary converging on commit.
forks.risk: Mode-dependent grammar can make body shape, effect classification and error precedence ambiguous to users and tools.
evidenceRequired: HIR region schema with mode and ownership facts

forks.hypothesis: Represent control nodes or sent code in a bounded IR so a pipeline can carry remote branch/loop behavior.
forks.promotionRule: Reject unless bounded IR, capability, isolation, cancellation, security and provider evidence proves the representation without hidden general execution.
forks.risk: Sent control can hide an unbounded remote program, alter authority and make commit/error behavior non-local.

forks.hypothesis: Keep transaction as a separate source keyword and let pipeline remain a static DAG with return.
forks.tradeoff: Preserves clear body-shape and atomicity signals, but retains two source concepts and duplicates some tooling/runtime machinery.

rules.policy: A query-only pipeline never produces unknownOutcome.
rules.requiredEvidence: Effect classifier and provider receipt must prove that no mutation can commit.

rules.policy: An idempotent or reconcilable mutation requires an EffectId that is retained across retry and reconciliation.
rules.requiredEvidence: Provider deduplication or reconciliation receipt and typed output ownership.

rules.policy: A non-idempotent mutation must be transactional or be rejected.
rules.requiredEvidence: Atomic provider contract, or a diagnostic that rejects the effect before dispatch.

rules.policy: Without a provider admission or receipt fact, a lost acknowledgement before node admission remains typed uncertainty; if the provider proves non-admission, the outcome is known and retry is safe only under the contract.
rules.requiredEvidence: Transport transcript and provider status query.

rules.policy: Without a provider admission or receipt fact, a lost acknowledgement after a node may have run remains unknownOutcome; a provider proof of non-admission makes the outcome known, otherwise no blind retry.

Without a provider admission or receipt fact, a lost commit acknowledgement remains unknownCommit or the corresponding typed uncertainty; a provider proof of non-admission makes the outcome known, and otherwise it never becomes rollback or silent success.
rules.requiredEvidence: Commit/ACK fault injection and provider acknowledgement oracle.

adversarialCases.expected: idempotent/reconcilable mutation retains EffectId across retry and reconciliation
non-idempotent mutation is transactional or rejected before dispatch
without provider admission/receipt fact, lost ACK before node admission remains typed uncertainty; proven non-admission is known and safely retryable only under contract
without provider admission/receipt fact, lost ACK after node execution preserves unknownOutcome; proven non-admission is known
without provider admission/receipt fact, lost ACK before commit confirmation preserves unknownCommit; proven non-admission is known
without provider admission/receipt fact, lost ACK after a possible commit never becomes an asserted rollback
cancel requests stop admission and every path drains children, providers and in-flight responses
body, cancellation, transport and commit uncertainty use a documented precedence without hiding uncertainty
capabilities, output envelope ownership and effect ownership remain explicit at each node
multi-provider and nested regions are rejected or explicitly contracted; no distributed transaction is inferred
branch on remote result is classified as region/control evidence, not silently accepted as a static DAG edge
isolation/access/provider defaults are visible in the contract or diagnostic, never ambient
w explain reports source mode, effect, uncertainty, provider receipt and ownership
